_comment: SHARED. The 10 WCAG 2.2 criteria, in display order, grouped by who they affect most. Edit only by agreement.

1.1.1.name: Non-text Content
1.1.1.check: A text label names the CAPTCHA's purpose, and a non-visual alternative exists.

1.3.1.name: Info and Relationships
1.3.1.check: Instructions and inputs are tied together for screen readers.

1.4.4.name: Resize Text
1.4.4.check: The CAPTCHA is still usable at 200% zoom.

2.1.1.name: Keyboard
2.1.1.check: Every step works with Tab, Enter, Space and the arrow keys only.

2.2.1.name: Timing Adjustable
2.2.1.check: Time limits can be extended or are long enough.

2.5.7.name: Dragging Movements
2.5.7.check: There is a way to finish without dragging.

2.5.8.name: Target Size (Minimum)
2.5.8.check: Clickable targets are at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels.

3.3.8.name: Accessible Authentication (Minimum)
3.3.8.check: On a login, there is a path that needs no puzzle-solving.

4.1.2.name: Name, Role, Value
4.1.2.check: Controls are announced correctly in VoiceOver.

pass.label: Pass
pass.meaning: Meets the criterion for screen-reader and keyboard-only users in our testing.

partial.label: Partial
partial.meaning: Meets it only on some paths, only when the site owner turns an option on, or with significant friction.

fail.label: Fail
fail.meaning: Does not meet the criterion; a screen-reader or keyboard-only user is blocked or has no working alternative.
